comment:
Agent with full artifacts pipeline:
  - generate_image: creates an image AND auto-registers it in AttachmentRegistry.
  - load_attachment: lets the LLM 'see' a previously generated image (vision input on the next turn).
  - http_post_image: POSTs an image to a webhook using $attachment:<id> in the body — the engine resolves the placeholder to a data: URI before sending.
Demonstrates capabilities 1+2+3 from the artifacts unification design. Requires DATABASE_URL + OPENAI_API_KEY.

test_payload.prompt: Genera una imagen de un perrito con gorra azul. Después abrila para revisar lo que generaste y describime brevemente qué ves. Si la imagen está OK, mándala a https://httpbin.org/post.

config.system_message: Three tools available: generate_image, load_attachment (auto-injected by the engine), http_post_image. Workflow: (1) call generate_image with a detailed prompt to create the image. (2) call load_attachment with the resulting attachment_id to inspect what you created — vision will let you describe it on the next turn. (3) call http_post_image with the destination URL and a body that contains the placeholder '$attachment:<the_attachment_id>'. The engine resolves the placeholder to a data: URI before sending the request, so you never see the raw bytes. Always invoke tools directly; never describe what you're about to do in plain text first.

generate_image.name: generate_image
generate_image.description: Generate an image from a prompt. Returns { images: [{ attachment_id, url, mime_type, ... }] }. Save the attachment_id to use it later with load_attachment or http_post_image.

http_post_image.name: http_post_image
http_post_image.description: POST a previously-generated image to a webhook URL. The body's `image` field MUST be the literal string '$attachment:<attachment_id>' where <attachment_id> is from a previous generate_image call — e.g. '$attachment:gen-att-xyz'. The engine reads bytes from storage and replaces the placeholder with 'data:image/png;base64,...' before the request goes out.

image.description: The string '$attachment:<attachment_id>' — the engine resolves it to data: URI.
